reason: Re-opened packet.js pali 4: Story IV.5 (Niggardly Kosiya) carries the evidence verbatim, the Teacher in the Hall of Truth: a monk who would convert a household without impairing faith, without impairing riches ... must approach that household to make known the virtues of the Buddha as a bee approaches a flower; it follows the [374] marker and precedes the stanza, and the next marker is [376] after the stanza (Burlingame omits the word explanation), so Norman p. 374 holds; Book IV is in vol. 2 (HOS 29). The Pali Tattha agrees (Na hi tassa gāme caraṇapaccayā kulānaṃ saddhāhāni vā bhogahāni vā honti). The paraphrase (the monk who wins a household over, making the Buddha’s virtues known without impairing its faith or riches) says no more than the words. Plain sense true to day.js: 47 and 48 are on death carrying off the distracted man gathering flowers, and 49 is the first verse on the sage; no four-word run from the key. Not Müller’s. verse.js ok (Dhammapada 49, at 48, 24 words); entry-check ok, no warnings.
